correctness.rationale: Let N be projective-point to k-subspace incidence, v=[n]_q, r=[k]_q, B=#Gr_q(n,k). Transitivity on ordered distinct projective points gives Gram N*N=aI+bJ with a=Br(v-r)/(v(v-1))>0, so H_{<=1}=ran N has dimension v and contains constants. On the P0-star, point columns identify with quotient projective points of V/P0 (q lifts each), so RN has rank v'=[n-1]_q; its mean-zero permutation constituent is irreducible over C by double transitivity. Compression S=RPR* acts as scalar on that constituent and as 1 on constants because 1_A is itself an incidence column. Trace of P M_A P is [k]_q, giving theta=([k]_q-1)/([n-1]_q-1)=[k-1]_q/[n-2]_q; zero eigenspace has dimension v-v'=q^(n-1). For k=n-1, theta=1 correctly merges eigenvalue multiplicities. Nonzero singular values and optimal minimum-energy extension norm follow from the singular-value theorem. Independently recomputed finite q=2,3 trace/rank identities; finite q<=4 checker cannot prove all-prime-power theorem, but proof does.
